name: Region X
summary: Region X runs guided sea kayak, walking and kayak camping trips from Batemans Bay on the NSW South Coast. Short tours include oyster tasting on the Clyde River, glass bottom kayaks in a marine sanctuary and a sunset pizza paddle. They also hire kayaks at Mossy Point and lead longer journeys in Murramarang National Park and further afield.
standouts: Running kayak trips around Batemans Bay since 2006
Supports seabird breeding field science and runs marine debris kayak clean-ups

trips.title: Oyster Tasting Kayak Tour – Batemans Bay
trips.summary: A two hour guided paddle on the Clyde River estuary that stops at a working oyster farm. You meet the growers, watch a shucking demonstration and taste several oyster varieties, then paddle through the leases and the 'Oyster Village'. The paddling distance is short and suits most ages and abilities.
highlights: Meet a 4th generation oyster farmer
Oyster tasting and a shucking demonstration
Paddle through the oyster leases of the Clyde River
Short paddle in double sea kayaks

includes: A selection of oysters for oyster tasting

trips.title: Glass Bottom Kayak Tour, Batemans Bay
trips.summary: A two hour family tour in stable double kayaks fitted with clear portholes, in the Cullendulla Creek marine sanctuary just north of Batemans Bay. Guides help you spot stingrays, crabs, fish and birds, and talk about how First Nations people used the area. Snacks are shared in the mangroves or on the sand flats, depending on the tide.

Cullendulla Creek Nature Reserve marine sanctuary
Suited to first time kayakers and families
Snacks included

trips.title: Pizza Paddle – Sunset Kayak Tour
trips.summary: A two hour guided paddle on the Clyde River at sunset, with pizza from a Batemans Bay waterfront restaurant delivered to your kayak. After dinner the guide leads you into the Clyde River National Park after dark and talks about local history, oyster farming, gold and timber. Vegetarian, vegan and gluten free options are available.

Sunset and after dark paddle on the Clyde River

Vegetarian, vegan and gluten free options

trips.title: Half Day Sea Kayak Tour, Batemans Bay
trips.summary: A five hour guided sea kayak trip along the Batemans Bay coastline in double sit-in sea kayaks, split into two easy legs. You stop in a sheltered cove for a morning tea picnic with time to snorkel, swim or walk. The route changes with the conditions, and migrating whales can be seen in season.
highlights: Two kayak legs split by a morning tea picnic
Optional snorkel, gear provided (no wetsuits)
Seals, dolphins and migrating whales in season
Route chosen on the day to suit conditions

trips.title: Sea Kayak Tollgate Islands
trips.summary: A five hour guided paddle for people who have kayaked before, crossing about an hour of open water to the protected Tollgate Islands off Batemans Bay. You circle the islands to see cliffs, grottos and seabird colonies, as landing is not allowed, then rest at a mainland beach for morning tea. The trip finishes by midday.

Caves, grottos and overhung ledges
Seabirds including little penguins
Morning tea picnic on a mainland beach

trips.title: Snorkel from a kayak – Batemans Bay
trips.summary: A three hour trip in sit-on-top kayaks to a sheltered reef or shoreline, where the guides anchor the kayaks and you slide in to snorkel. Expect kelp, fish, urchins, rays and sometimes seals, then hot drinks and muffins afterwards. Wetsuits and snorkel gear are supplied, and non-swimmers can join if they keep their life jacket on.
highlights: Snorkel from anchored kayaks
Kelp forest and cold water marine life
Water from about 16 degrees in winter to about 22 in April
Hot drink and snack included

trips.departsFrom: Varies with conditions, generally within 20km of Batemans Bay; confirmed by phone or SMS the afternoon before

trips.checkNotes: Wetsuit is not in the 'Package Includes' list but the itinerary and homepage say wetsuits are provided. Visibility depends on wind, rain, swell and tides.

trips.summary: A guided day trip from Canberra to the coast, travelling through Bungendore and Braidwood. You see the kangaroos at Pebbly Beach in Murramarang National Park, have free time for lunch in Batemans Bay, then join the oyster tasting kayak tour on the Clyde River before returning to Canberra.
highlights: Pickup from the Canberra CBD
Kangaroos at Pebbly Beach, Murramarang National Park
Oyster tasting kayak tour on the Clyde River
Back in Canberra around 5:30 to 6pm

trips.summary: A guided day walk on the Murramarang National Park coast, starting at South Durras, over rock platforms, cliff tops and long beaches. The group crosses Durras Lake on foot or by kayak and stops for a picnic lunch and a swim. Hotel transfers from Batemans Bay are included.

Morning tea and picnic lunch

trips.title: Day Walk – Pigeon House Mountain Morton National Park
trips.summary: A guided summit hike up Pigeon House Mountain in Morton National Park, with transfers from Batemans Bay or Ulladulla. The track is steep at the start and finishes with steel ladders to the summit, which looks over the Budawang wilderness and the coast. Afterwards the group swims in the upper Clyde River and has lunch.

Swim stop on the upper Clyde River
Morning tea and lunch included

Guides cook all meals and supply tents and mattresses, and the afternoon is free for walking, snorkelling or swimming. The route is chosen on the weather and the campsites have few or no facilities.

Paddlers camp on beaches, stay in island villages and snorkel reefs, with daily paddles of about 11 to 20km, and finish at a resort with a chance to snorkel with manta rays. Suited to people with paddling experience and fit, active beginners.
